scope: Read-only review of the frozen diagnostic resource output and independent schema-only boundary probes under both locked Python environments. No generator, public runtime, product tests, source, generated resource, fixture, Git, network, connector or Vault mutation was performed by this review.
verdict: The diagnostic generation itself completed safely and its byte/reference audit passed, but the generated resources fail four contract groups. Both Python 3.12 and 3.13 independently reproduced the same 16 mismatches out of 34 checks: four direct repository-component cases and nine embedded GitHub locator cases from one repository-regex boundary defect, plus the minimum bundle-directory case, the maximum JSON Pointer oracle and the maximum-source exclusive column oracle. The output remains diagnostic-only and is not eligible for installation or product acceptance.

findings.observed: _OWNER_INPUT/_OWNER_SAVED and _NAME_INPUT/_NAME_SAVED use negative lookaheads ending in \Z while the same component regex is embedded before /repo suffixes or /commit, /blob and raw path suffixes.
findings.impact: ./repo and ../repo are admitted as repository_input and repository_saved because the lookahead sees a slash before end-of-string. owner/name.git is admitted in all three URL definitions because the .git lookahead sees the locator suffix after the repository name. R9 requires exact dot/dot-dot components to be rejected and the name to reject a case-insensitive .git suffix in these embedded forms.
findings.required_correction: Make component exclusions terminate at a component boundary (slash or end), and apply the .git suffix exclusion at the repository-name boundary in both standalone and embedded URL grammars. Add direct and all three URL positive/negative probes.

findings.observed: bundle_directory is constrained by _CHECKOUT_REL, which applies the existing batch-id _SEGMENT grammar to every component, and then has minLength=8.
findings.contract_basis: R3 requires a canonical relative raw input bundle path below checkout .work, with no symlink, lexical alias, exact dot/dot-dot component or replaced marker; R6 repeats canonical checkout-relative .work/... spelling. Neither contract constrains every input-directory component to the batch-id grammar.
clear_additional_narrowing: .work/input.v1 is a non-alias relative directory spelling containing a dot and is excluded by _SEGMENT.
.work/_input and .work/-input have ordinary non-alias components with leading underscore/hyphen and are excluded by _SEGMENT.
.work/input_ and .work/input- have ordinary non-alias components with trailing underscore/hyphen and are excluded by _SEGMENT.
findings.impact: The one-character valid path is rejected by minLength, and otherwise canonical input directories with portable dot/underscore/hyphen components are rejected by the unqualified reuse of batch-id syntax. The output namespace's batch grammar is explicitly scoped to .work/<batch>/code-evidence-v1; it does not authorize narrowing arbitrary raw input bundle directory components.
findings.required_correction: Separate the input bundle path component grammar from the output batch-id grammar according to the frozen R3/R6 path contract, while preserving exact dot/dot-dot, alias, symlink and checkout-relative checks; remove the redundant minimum or set it to the true shortest spelling. Add positive probes for .work/a and representative dot/underscore/hyphen components.

findings.oracle: The pinned accepted oracle is 33 nodes at depth 32 with a valid maximum pointer of 16416 characters (oracle SHA-256 f676a37634ecf854b54bd43135a3028cb9a264bc6d532a103638d2c22f67b959, 582590 bytes).
findings.impact: The generated common definition maxLength=16384 rejects the complete accepted config_result and cascades into child/declaration pointer references.
findings.required_correction: Raise the pointer bound to at least the accepted 16416-character value with documented derivation/headroom and add a positive/negative boundary probe.

findings.oracle: The pinned accepted oracle uses a 262144-byte source and one-based exclusive column_end=262145 (oracle SHA-256 c56de0f267881dfe277a280619923e9f625fd0ce82b5119e619534fa5e51d407, 1785 bytes).
findings.impact: The generated span definition caps column_end at 262144, rejecting a valid maximum-source config_result; the probe's additional oneOf leaves are cascading diagnostics from this mismatch.
findings.required_correction: Permit column_end through 262145 while retaining the source byte maximum and add positive maximum-source plus true over-boundary probes.

non_findings.generation_and_reference_integrity: Both locked-Python byte/reference audits resolved 314 references and agreed on profile/resource bytes; this does not establish semantic boundary correctness.
non_findings.probe_scope: The independent probe is schema-only and explicitly makes no public runtime, saved-byte identity, filesystem workflow or product acceptance claim.
non_findings.resource_mutation_guard: Both boundary executions report resource pins unchanged before and after.

required_next_step: Freeze a repair-only R2 generator/test package addressing all four findings, regenerate into a fresh absent diagnostic root, replay the same schema-only probes on both locked Pythons, and retain the prior R1 output/evidence unchanged.
